function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection directly from here, but you can quickly find out your current download/upload speeds with a few simple steps. Below are a couple of common methods—pick the one that fits your setup best.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick Browser Test (easiest)

1. Open a web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, etc.).  
2. Go to <https://www.speedtest.net> (or <https://fast.com> for a very quick test).  
3. Click “Go” or “Start” and wait a few seconds.  
4. The page will display your **download** and **upload** speeds, plus ping.

> **Tip:** If you’re on a mobile device, the same sites work fine—just tap the “Go” button.

---

## 2️⃣ Command‑Line Test (for Linux/macOS/Windows PowerShell)

If you prefer a terminal or need to script the test, you can use the official `speedtest-cli` tool.

### a. Install `speedtest-cli`

| OS | Install Command |
|----|-----------------|
| **Linux** (Ubuntu/Debian) | `sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli` |
| **macOS** (Homebrew) | `brew install speedtest-cli` |
| **Windows** (PowerShell) | `pip install speedtest-cli` (requires Python & pip) |

> **Note:** If you already have it installed, skip to the next step.

### b. Run the Test

```bash
speedtest
```

This will output something like:

```
Testing from Your ISP (Your City)...
Retrieving speedtest.net configuration...
Testing download speed........................................
Download:  85.23 Mbit/s
Testing upload speed..........................................
Upload:    12.45 Mbit/s
```

---

## 3️⃣ Using the Built‑in Windows Tool (Optional)

Windows 10/11 includes a built‑in “Network Speed Test” in the Settings app:

1. Open **Settings** → **Network & Internet** → **Status**.  
2. Click **Network Speed Test** (if available).  
3. It will launch a web‑based test similar to Speedtest.net.

---

## 4️⃣ Want me to run a test for you? (Optional)

If you’re comfortable running a command and have `speedtest-cli` installed, I can execute it for you right now. Just let me know, and I’ll fire it up. (I’ll use the `cmd_controller_execute` tool to run the command.)

---

### Quick Summary

| Method | When to Use | How to Run |
|--------|-------------|------------|
| Browser (Speedtest.net) | Anyone, any device | Visit site, click “Go” |
| Command‑line (`speedtest-cli`) | Developers, scripting | `speedtest` |
| Windows Settings | Windows 10/11 | Settings → Network Speed Test |

Let me know which route you’d like to take, or if you’d like me to run the command for you!
